facts.claim: "High on Weed" is a one-track single by Waylon Napadogan, released February 22, 2023, running 3:06.
Apple Music lists the single under the Rock genre, with a 2023 copyright line (℗) to Waylon Napadogan, who is also the label.
Waylon Napadogan is a musician and comedian from New Brunswick, Canada.

Before "High on Weed", he released the single "Oh Ya No For Sure Bud" (Dec 2, 2021), the six-track EP "I Seen a Sasquatch" (Jul 22, 2022), and the single "No Wonder Sharon Took the Kids and Left My Ass Again" (Nov 18, 2022).
After "High on Weed" he released "Stuck in a Porta Potty" (Sep 12, 2023), "98 Pontiac Sunfire" (Nov 2023), and "2008 Ford Ranger" (Aug 20, 2024).
His latest release as of the sources is the single "Lot Lizard", dated July 5, 2025.
He appeared as a comedy singer and pianist on America's Got Talent Season 17. He was eliminated at the audition stage after performing an original song about naming a baby Gary.

In a Strange Grooves podcast interview he discussed how he got into music, his early influences, how he used TikTok and Instagram to build an audience, and where the ideas for his viral songs come from.

He has described writing "Frig Off Bud", which he calls probably his oldest song, at age seven as a defence against school bullies. Grid City Magazine linked him to the mullet-era 90s New Country sound.
He markets his songs on TikTok as comedy and country music, and describes his music as Canadian.

research.lineage: Napadogan's songs sit in the Atlantic Canadian comedy-country tradition, with 90s New Country-style songwriting and humour about Maritime working-class life, spread largely through TikTok and Instagram.

draft:
A palm-muted guitar riff, distorted and fast, chugs under **High on Weed** like an engine that won't idle down. Bass doubles the drive, the snare and kick hit hard, and a steady hi-hat keeps everything locked. Nothing drops out, nothing builds. The band just stays in the pocket and keeps pushing.

That steadiness is the joke's delivery system. Waylon Napadogan is a musician and comedian from New Brunswick, and he markets his songs on TikTok as comedy and country. This one Apple Music files under Rock, and you can hear why: the riff owes more to a garage than to a honky-tonk. But the songwriting instinct is the same one running through his catalogue, which reads like a list of things a Maritime guy might say out loud, own, or get stuck in: "Oh Ya No For Sure Bud," "I Seen a Sasquatch," "No Wonder Sharon Took the Kids and Left My Ass Again," "Stuck in a Porta Potty," "98 Pontiac Sunfire," "2008 Ford Ranger." The titles are the punchlines and the premises at once. "High on Weed" is as blunt as any of them. It names a state of being and doesn't apologize for it.

The vocal is clear, mid-range, a little nasal, with no harmonies stacked behind it. It's conversational and rhythmic, riding the beat like someone telling a story at speed rather than performing one. The production is dry and tight, a little raw around the edges, the sound of a few people playing close together rather than a studio dressing them up. Napadogan is his own label here, and the record sounds like it: direct, unfussed, built to land on a phone speaker and get shared.

There's a feeling underneath the bit worth taking seriously. Napadogan has said he wrote "Frig Off Bud," probably his oldest song, at seven, as a defence against school bullies. That's a kid learning that a funny song can be armour, that you can say the rough thing first and set the terms. He carried that instinct onto the America's Got Talent stage with an original about naming a baby Gary, and into an audience built on TikTok and Instagram. "High on Weed" comes out of the same place: the plain pleasure of saying the unpolished thing in a loud room and watching people laugh with you instead of at you.

It sticks because the band plays it completely straight, so you're grinning at the title and nodding along to the riff before you've decided whether it's a joke.
